title: Make room in centre
objective: Challenge the centre and bring a knight to a useful square.

commentary_source.name: Uroschess original synthetic lesson
commentary_source.attribution: Original instructional text and practice line inspired by a Scotch Game idea

steps.explanation: Both sides have a pawn in the middle. White can ask Black's pawn a question.
steps.detail: Move the d-pawn forward to challenge e5. If Black takes it, a knight can take back.
steps.coach_prompt: Make room for your pieces in the middle.

question.prompt: Which pawn can challenge Black's pawn in the middle?
hints: Try moving it two squares, to d4.

children.feedback: Black took your pawn. Look for a way to take it back.
children.next_prompt: Black took your pawn. Which knight can take it back?
hints: Your knight on f3 can take the pawn on d4.

children.feedback: Your knight takes back the pawn and reaches the centre.
Black's knight on c6 can take your queen right away. Find a safer piece to take the pawn.

tree.feedback: d3 supports your pawn, but it does not challenge Black's pawn yet. Try moving farther.

question.other_legal_move_text: That move may be useful too. Explore it, then return to try the central pawn idea.

takeaway: A pawn challenge can open space. Bring a piece into the centre when you take back.
